newsitem.title: UK: Graham Greene archives to be sold at auction.
newsitem.headline: Graham Greene archives to be sold at auction.

text.p: An archive of private papers and other memorabilia relating to the late British author Graham Greene are to be sold at auction next month in what is expected to be one of the biggest literary events for years.

The papers, ranging from Greene's contributions to his school magazine and an unfinished novel he gave away only weeks before his death, are expected to fetch some 250,000 pounds ($420,000), auctioneers Sotheby's said on Tuesday.
Greene, hailed as one of the 20th century's greatest novelists, died in 1991 at the age of 86.
The collection includes Greene's proof copy of his novel "The End of the Affair" and books containing inscriptions from Greene to his wife Vivien and to two of his lovers.
Other papers in the December 16 sale in London include Greene's own set of photocopies of his FBI file.

As a student, Greene was briefly a member of the Communist Party, which caused him problems later in obtaining U.S. visas. Ironically, he later worked for Britain's MI6 spy agency during the Second World War -- an experience that he drew on in many subsequent novels.
The archive of annotated books, manuscripts and letters were collected by New York book dealer Clinton Ives Smullyan.
